nodes.label: Daily Cycle (4-Stage State Machine)
nodes.rationale: Described as a 4-stage state machine, but the source lists 'Closing Phase' twice (stage 3, and an expanded stage 4 'Daily Reviews & Ledger'); likely a drafting duplication rather than a distinct fourth stage. Flagged for review.

nodes.label: Dynamic Phase-Based Music System
nodes.rationale: Music follows the gameplay phase to control pacing: calm acoustic coastal tracks in the Main Menu and Prep reinforce that time is paused, an upbeat bustling track in Open matches the chaos, and a reflective track in Closing accompanies the ledger.

nodes.label: Museum Quality Meter (0-100%)
nodes.rationale: Stars are driven by an active Quality percentage instead of being earned passively, so progression reflects how well the player builds, maintains and behaves. Reaching 100% grants a half-star and resets with a tougher threshold; Quality floors at 0%, and low Quality cuts customer spawn rates and daily profits.

nodes.label: Walkie-Talkie Alert System
nodes.rationale: Lets the player keep mining during the Open shift without being overwhelmed: incident alerts let them sprint back to handle it or finish the mining trip for a minor penalty; keeps the Open Phase lively but not overly fast-paced.

nodes.label: Act 1: The Washed-Up Dream
nodes.rationale: Rags-to-riches start: zero money and no daily rent; mine beach gems and ores to fund the first tools and exhibits.

nodes.label: Across-the-Street Equipment Shop
nodes.rationale: Tools are bought by physically walking across the street to a storefront rather than from a menu screen; stock stays basic until the Better Equipment upgrade is purchased.

nodes.label: Core Gameplay Loop
nodes.rationale: A stress-free preparation phase is balanced by a high-stakes financial economy; time only passes once the player flips the Open sign, so strategizing happens entirely at the player's own pace.

nodes.label: Dual Economy Tension
nodes.rationale: Every dig forces an inventory choice: sell gems/ores for short-term cash (jumpstart from zero, pay wages, avoid debt, fund tools) or display fossils for long-term prestige (permanently higher ticket revenue and attraction).

nodes.label: Simplified Digging Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Keeps development scope manageable and avoids complicated terrain deformation: digging is an interact button on a spawn node, a quick animation, and an RNG drop table.

nodes.label: Prep Phase (Time Paused)
nodes.rationale: Time is paused so the player can dig, prep fossils, arrange exhibits and buy upgrades without pressure.

nodes.label: Upgrade Points (Research & Mastery Points)
nodes.rationale: A progression currency kept separate from cash: cash buys physical tools and pays bills, while Upgrade Points unlock tree nodes.

nodes.label: Precision Fossil Cleaning Mini-Game (Indoor Lab)
nodes.rationale: Raw rock-encased fossils are cleaned at the indoor workbench; higher precision yields a better Preservation Rating, which raises the ticket price guests will pay.

nodes.label: Skill Tree
nodes.rationale: Replaces multiple underground mine levels as the progression structure: the large coastline's richer zones are blocked off until unlocked with Upgrade Points.

nodes.label: Multi-Tier Upgrade Tree
nodes.rationale: Multi-tier tree for expanding the shack into an educational empire; nodes (building expansions, Better Equipment stock) cost Upgrade Points rather than cash. The document uses both 'Upgrade Tree' and 'Skill Tree', possibly for the same system.

nodes.label: Top-Down Build Mode
nodes.rationale: Switches the camera to a top-down grid view of the floor plan so exhibits, attractions, concessions and decorations can be placed, rotated and rearranged without first/third-person camera clutter.

nodes.label: Player Conduct & Physics Ragdoll
nodes.rationale: Comedic physics lets the player hit or ragdoll unruly guests and employees, but assaulting innocent customers produces scathing reviews that tank Quality, so behaviour carries consequences.

nodes.label: Stylized Mid-Poly Cel-Shaded Visual Style
nodes.rationale: Charming, smooth cel-shading and vibrant lighting that keep distinct geometric shapes without becoming overly realistic.

nodes.label: Modular Settings Menu
nodes.rationale: Separate tabs: Audio (master/music/SFX sliders), Gameplay (auto-cleaning toggles, text speed), Graphics (resolution, window mode, shadow quality) and Controls (full remapping).

nodes.label: Tide & Trove (Incremental Museum Simulator GDD)
nodes.rationale: Core premise: a zero-budget aspiring paleontologist buys an abandoned museum on a fossil-rich coastline armed only with a shovel, and must dig, prepare and display fossils to save the cove from bankruptcy while paying staff wages and upkeep. Genre: incremental / management simulator.

nodes.label: The Secret of Ammonite Bay (Narrative Arc)
nodes.norm_label: the secret of ammonite bay (narrative arc)
nodes.rationale: The narrative gives the player a compelling reason to keep expanding the museum beyond pure monetary gains.

nodes.label: Optional Exhibit Plaque Builder
nodes.rationale: Every exhibit gets a default plaque that satisfies normal guests; manually choosing Era, Diet and Habitat tags earns an Educational Accuracy bonus.

nodes.label: Research Assistant
nodes.rationale: Mentioned in the Fossil Enthusiasts entry as a hire who fills in plaque tags; likely the same role as the Paleontology Intern named in the educational section.

nodes.label: Opt-In Educational Mechanics
nodes.rationale: Real-world paleontology is an optional, rewarding layer: engaging grants extra cash and bonuses, while players who only want museum chaos and loot can bypass or automate it with zero penalty.

nodes.label: Real Geological Strata (Cenozoic / Mesozoic / Paleozoic)
nodes.rationale: Beach zones and rock layers reflect authentic eras so players learn which creatures coexisted through visual discovery, without forced quizzes or text walls.
